 Is the Bitcoin four-year cycle real? Explained by a quant. A thousand dollars turned into 23 million simply by buying Bitcoin here and selling it here. Every four years. Three times in a row. This is the rainbow chart. Blue means cheap. Red means bubble. These lines are the harvings. Every four years, Bitcoin's code cuts the number of new coins in half. The story. After each harvying, the price climbs the rainbow. A year after the top, it crashes. Then it repeats. And for three cycles, it worked. Each top came 12 to 18 months after a harvying. Up about 95 times. In 30, then 8. Each crash wiped out more than three quarters. And the tops? Almost exactly four years apart. So is the cycle real? Or is it astrology for men? A quant's first question. Could luck do this? The harvying is the one date everyone knows in advance. So we compared buying on each harvying with buying on any other day. 18 months later, the first three beat nearly nine in 10 days. Pick three random days and the odds of doing that well are under one in a hundred. Luck rarely does that. And here's the catch. The cycle story gets drawn after the fact. In 2022, the price fell out of the bottom of the rainbow. So its maker added a new color, then drew a new rainbow. Even the maker says you can't predict Bitcoin with one. And crashes that don't fit get left out. April 2013, down more than 70% from a record off schedule. And the push behind the cycle keeps shrinking. In 2012, the harvying cut new coins worth 12.5% of all Bitcoin a year. By 2024, under 1%. Same cut, much smaller push. So the fourth harvying. The top came on time in October 2025. But almost everything else broke. Bitcoin hit a record before the harvying. A first. The gain after? The smallest yet. About two times. The crash? The smallest so far. About half. And our test? 18 months after this harvying, buying that day beat fewer than half of all days. And the bottom cycle watches circled for October 6th. So far, the low came in July. So is the cycle real? Three times it beat the odds. But its push is shrinking. And the fourth time, it broke. Three in a row is a streak, not a law. Comment below if you want us to send you the data.
